primitives.name: Position-based punt necessitation
primitives.verbatim_quote: 80 WINNING FOOTBALL course, it is necessitated by the position of the ball with regard to the side-lines or goal-posts.
primitives.assumptions: Ball location relative to sidelines and goalposts dictates punt necessity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Absolute sideline/goalpost boundary triggers punt necessity.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI probability calibration: punt necessity as conditioned event given spatial state. Maps to GSE state-transition logic: punt action triggered by boundary state.

primitives.name: First-down punt fallacy
primitives.verbatim_quote: This is very far indeed from saying that a punt on the first down is the inevitable play for these conditions.
primitives.assumptions: First-down punts are not inherently optimal; they represent a strategic misconception.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Monotonicity trap where predictable first-down punting creates exploitable patterns.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI overconfidence correction: avoiding predictable strategies reduces information leakage. Maps to GSE exploitability minimization: predictable actions create adversarial opportunities.
layer2.telemetry: Punt frequency variance across downs as empirical indicator.

primitives.name: Policy monotony aversion
primitives.verbatim_quote: To my mind it is exactly the reverse and I should play it, if I were a quarter, only often enough to avoid a foreseeable monotony of policy-which, after all, is the one fatal and hopeless defect in offensive football.
primitives.assumptions: Strategic unpredictability prevents long-term exploitation by opponents.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Predictable policy leads to catastrophic loss of strategic advantage.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI conformal prediction: randomized strategy introduces uncertainty bounds. Maps to GSE state-disruption: introducing randomness breaks predictable opponent state-estimates.
layer2.telemetry: Strategy entropy or unpredictability scores as empirical measure.

primitives.name: Down-based punt advisability
primitives.verbatim_quote: The punt becomes, of course, advisable on the third down and almost inevitable on the fourth, but the first two plays, it seems to me, should never be such that the enemy can count with any degree of certainty on their being adopted.
primitives.assumptions: Punt probability increases monotonically with down number due to diminishing offensive options.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fourth down punt inevitability arises from near-zero offensive success likelihood.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI sequential testing: higher down numbers increase evidence threshold for retaining possession. Maps to GSE transition kernel: down-number state influences action probabilities via conditional likelihoods.
layer2.telemetry: Down-specific punt rates as empirical calibration data.
